name: Ajogun, Ese
body:
ESE
CR 5

This strange person shifts in appearance from callow youth to wizened elder before your eyes, and his clothes likewise shift from humble peasant garb to regal vestments.

XP 1,600
LN Medium outsider (ajogun, lawful, native, shapechanger)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +13

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 16, flat-footed 12 (+4 Dex, +2 insight)
hp 51 (6d10+18)
Fort +5, Ref +9, Will +7; Immune polymorph effects aside from its own

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee dagger +8/+3 (1d4+2/19–20)
Special Attacks rebalancing misdeeds (DC 19), major inconvenience, minor inconvenience (DC 17), minor accident (DC 17)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 6th; concentration +10)

Constant—nondetection (DC 17)

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 18, Con 16, Int 13, Wis 15, Cha 19
Base Atk +6; CMB +8; CMD 24
Feats Ability Focus (rebalancing misdeeds), Alertness, Deceitful
Skills Bluff +15, Diplomacy +10, Disguise +12, Intimidate +10, Perception +13, Sense Motive +4, Sleight of Hand +10, Stealth +13
Languages Abyssal, Common
SQ change shape (medium sized young or old male humanoids only, alter self)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Rebalancing Misdeeds (Su)

One creature within 150 feet that an ese can see must succeed at a DC 19 Will save or becomes the focus of that ese’s rebalancing. The ese then decides whether the target is minorly imbalanced or a majorly imbalanced. The target receives a -2 penalty on any d20 rolls, similar to exhaustion. If the target is minorly imbalanced, the ese will usually stop focusing the next time the target falls below 50% hp during combat. If the target is majorly imbalanced, the ese will maintain their focus on the target until the next time they fall to 0 HP. While a creature is the focus of the ese’s rebalancing, the ese can sense the target’s general direction as though under the effects of a locate creature spell and has an idea of their activity (e.g. they would be able to tell that the target is resting, socializing, in danger, or in combat). The target is not aware of any attempt to afflict it with this ability; the only way to know is that the true face of the ese begins to show up in the creature’s dreams each night, getting more pronounced and frequent each night until it seems to be everywhere. and includes a +2 racial bonus.

Major Inconvenience (Su)

Once per round, when the focus of the ese’s rebalancing makes a d20 roll (e.g. attack roll, skill check, or save) while within 30 ft, the ese can cause them a major inconvenience. When they do, the target suffers -4 on the roll.

Minor Inconvenience (Su)

Once per round, when the focus of the ese’s rebalancing makes a d20 check (e.g. attack roll, skill check, or save) while within 150 ft, the ese can cause them a minor inconvenience. When they do, an additional issue arises from the check, regardless of success. Examples include: the bard makes a successful perform check and wins the king’s favor, but knocks over the queen regent immediately after and breaks her nose; a rogue picks a lock successfully, but accidentally slams the door open, causing a loud clang; the cleric successfully applies a bandage to a wounded soldier, but also drops their remaining bandages in the mud, making them useless. If no situational penalties seem applicable, the target is shaken for a minute (DC 17 Will negates).

Minor Accident (Ex)

Once per 10 minutes, the ese can cause a nearby shelf to collapse, a tree to fall, a small rockslide occur, or some other similar accident, injuring all creatures within 10 feet of the ese’s rebalancing focus. Creatures within the area take 6d6 bludgeoning damage as debris pummels the target and are pushed out of the area (DC 17 Reflex half and can choose where they end). If the ese is within this area, it takes only 1d6 damage but can choose to appear either as though it had succeeded or failed.

ECOLOGY

Environment Any
Organization usually solitary
Treasure standard

Ese are ajogun tasked with bringing balance to those who visit misfortune on others. They hunt or are tasked with bringing misfortune to those who have intentionally caused harm and take Advantage of their kin or community. To do so, they continually cause misfortune and other inflictions to the point that the target ends up seriously injured, or if the target realizes what happens, they may attempt to atone directly to the ese, usually with some sort of sacrifice. If successful, the ese may decide that the mortal has atoned and will depart. No one has ever figured out where all the sacrifices go; the ese have no need for wealth but generally will not turn down a sacrifice if it is large enough.

The ese has mastered blending in with mortals. Its true appearance is as a shadowy, smoky humanoid twisted and constantly warping. However, to accomplish their mission, the ese will shapeshift into either an old man or a young boy to avert suspicion and even request their targets aid or services to stay nearby. Many adventurers have unknowingly escorted an ese through the wilderness, only to meet their doom as the ese’s true purpose is revealed.
